subject: Fennec Fox
fact: Fennec foxes have very large ears that help release body heat.

subject: Kit Fox
fact: Kit foxes are small desert foxes with large ears and quick movements.

subject: Coyote
fact: Coyotes can live in deserts, grasslands, forests, and even cities.

subject: Bobcat
fact: Bobcats have short tails with dark tips and tufted ears.

subject: Mountain Lion
fact: Mountain lions can leap long distances with their powerful hind legs.

subject: Desert Bighorn Sheep
fact: Desert bighorn sheep can travel across steep rocky slopes with strong hooves.

subject: Pronghorn
fact: Pronghorns are among the fastest land mammals in North America.

subject: Black-Tailed Jackrabbit
fact: Jackrabbits use their long ears to help release heat.

subject: Desert Cottontail
fact: Desert cottontails rest in shade during the hottest parts of the day.

subject: Kangaroo Rat
fact: Kangaroo rats can survive with very little free water by getting moisture from seeds.

subject: Desert Woodrat
fact: Desert woodrats build large nests from sticks and plant material.

subject: Antelope Ground Squirrel
fact: Antelope ground squirrels can hold their tails over their backs like tiny sunshades.

subject: Meerkat
fact: Meerkats take turns watching for danger while the group searches for food.

subject: Dromedary Camel
fact: Dromedary camels have one hump that stores fat.

subject: Bactrian Camel
fact: Bactrian camels have two humps and can handle very cold deserts.

subject: Addax
fact: Addax antelope are adapted to hot dry deserts and can go long periods without drinking.

subject: Oryx
fact: Oryx have long straight horns and can tolerate high desert temperatures.

subject: Jerboa
fact: Jerboas hop on long hind legs and live in sandy deserts.

subject: Desert Hedgehog
fact: Desert hedgehogs curl into a spiny ball when threatened.

subject: Fat-Tailed Gerbil
fact: Fat-tailed gerbils store extra fat in their thick tails.

subject: Greater Roadrunner
fact: Roadrunners can run quickly on the ground and hunt small desert animals.

subject: Burrowing Owl
fact: Burrowing owls often live in underground burrows made by other animals.

subject: Cactus Wren
fact: Cactus wrens build bulky nests among thorny desert plants.

subject: Gambel's Quail
fact: Gambel's quail have a curved plume on top of their heads.

subject: Greater Sage-Grouse
fact: Male sage-grouse perform special dances at gathering places called leks.

subject: Gila Woodpecker
fact: Gila woodpeckers sometimes carve nest holes into giant saguaro cacti.

subject: Verdin
fact: Verdins build round nests with side entrances in desert shrubs.

subject: Elf Owl
fact: Elf owls are among the smallest owls in the world.

subject: Turkey Vulture
fact: Turkey vultures can find carrion partly by using a strong sense of smell.

subject: Golden Eagle
fact: Golden eagles use powerful talons to catch prey.

subject: Gila Monster
fact: Gila monsters are venomous lizards that spend much of their time underground.

subject: Desert Iguana
fact: Desert iguanas can stay active during very hot weather.

subject: Chuckwalla
fact: Chuckwallas wedge themselves into rock cracks and inflate their bodies when threatened.

subject: Collared Lizard
fact: Collared lizards can run on their hind legs for short distances.

subject: Horned Lizard
fact: Horned lizards have broad flat bodies covered with pointed scales.

subject: Fringe-Toed Lizard
fact: Fringe-toed lizards have special scales on their toes that help them move across loose sand.

subject: Sidewinder
fact: Sidewinders move sideways across loose sand and leave J-shaped tracks.

subject: Western Diamondback Rattlesnake
fact: Rattlesnakes warn threats by shaking special segments at the ends of their tails.

subject: Coachwhip Snake
fact: Coachwhips are fast nonvenomous snakes found in dry open habitats.

subject: Desert Tortoise
fact: Desert tortoises spend much of the year in burrows to avoid extreme heat and cold.

subject: Spadefoot Toad
fact: Spadefoot toads can remain underground for long dry periods and emerge after heavy rains.

subject: Sonoran Desert Toad
fact: Sonoran desert toads are large toads that become active during warm rainy weather.

subject: Desert Rain Frog
fact: Desert rain frogs have rounded bodies and live in sandy coastal deserts.

subject: Scorpion
fact: Scorpions use pincers and a curved stinger to capture prey and defend themselves.

subject: Desert Tarantula
fact: Desert tarantulas spend much of their time in burrows.

subject: Sun Spider
fact: Sun spiders are fast arachnids with large jaws but no venomous stinger.

subject: Darkling Beetle
fact: Some desert darkling beetles collect moisture from fog on their bodies.

subject: Sahara Silver Ant
fact: Sahara silver ants can forage briefly during extremely hot daytime conditions.

subject: Desert Locust
fact: Desert locusts can form enormous traveling swarms when conditions are right.

subject: Tarantula Hawk Wasp
fact: Tarantula hawk wasps hunt tarantulas to provide food for their young.

subject: Desert Honey Ant
fact: Some honey ants store sweet liquid in the swollen abdomens of special workers.

subject: Deathstalker Scorpion
fact: Deathstalker scorpions are pale desert scorpions adapted to dry regions.

subject: Ghost Crab
fact: Ghost crabs are fast-running shore crabs that live in burrows above the high-tide line on sandy beaches.

subject: Saharan Horned Viper
fact: Saharan horned vipers can bury themselves in sand with only their eyes exposed.

subject: Thorny Devil
fact: Thorny devils have grooved skin that can channel water toward their mouths.

subject: Perentie
fact: Perenties are large monitor lizards found in arid parts of Australia.

subject: Bilby
fact: Bilbies have long ears and dig deep spiral burrows in dry Australian habitats.

subject: Red Kangaroo
fact: Red kangaroos are well adapted to Australia's dry interior.

subject: Emu
fact: Emus can travel long distances in search of food and water.

subject: Arabian Sand Gazelle
fact: Arabian sand gazelles are slender desert antelope adapted to dry open landscapes.
